passages.text: ‘I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time. I will speak truthfully, not falsely. I will speak gently, not harshly. I will speak beneficially, not harmfully. I will speak lovingly, not from secret hate.’
passages.note: How to speak when you must confront or criticise someone

passages.text: ‘I must be parted and separated from all I hold dear and beloved.’
passages.note: Accepting that every loved thing will be lost

passages.text: ‘I am the owner of my deeds and heir to my deeds. Deeds are my womb, my relative, and my refuge. I shall be the heir of whatever deeds I do, whether good or bad.’ ‘As the days and nights pass by, what sort of person am I becoming?’
passages.note: Responsibility for one's actions; who am I becoming

passages.text: Suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and they check their own reflection in a clean bright mirror or a clear bowl of water. If they see any dirt or blemish there, they’d try to remove it. But if they don’t see any dirt or blemish there, they’re happy with that, as they’ve got all they wished for: ‘How fortunate that I’m clean!’ In the same way, checking is very helpful for a mendicant’s skillful qualities.
passages.note: Honest self-examination, like checking yourself in a mirror
